memoryText: For I delivered to you as of first importance what I also received: that Christ died for our sins in accordance with the Scriptures, that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day in accordance with the Scriptures.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read 1 Corinthians 15:3-4 slowly, several times, and try to say it from memory. Then read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This is a summary of the gospel, and it was handed down from the earliest days.

“As of first importance.” Paul places this message at the top of the list. Many things in the Christian life matter, but some matter most. The death and resurrection of Christ are the foundation.

“What I also received.” Paul did not invent the gospel. He received it, probably from the first apostles within a few years of the event, and he delivered it. We too receive and pass on.

“That Christ died for our sins.” Notice the three parts: the person (Christ), the event (died), and the purpose (for our sins). His death was not an accident but a substitution, dealing with our guilt.

“In accordance with the Scriptures.” The cross is the fulfillment of what the Old Testament promised, in Isaiah 53, Psalm 22, and the sacrifices.

“That he was buried.” The burial proves he truly died.

“That he was raised on the third day in accordance with the Scriptures.” The tomb was empty because Christ was alive. This too was foretold.

When the world offers other messages, say this verse. These two verses are the heart of what we believe.
weekInReview: This week you read the end of 1 Corinthians. Chapters 12 to 14 gave Paul’s teaching on spiritual gifts, the body of Christ, and the more excellent way of love, and a doctrinal pause considered the gifts and the unity of the body. Psalms 111 and 112 sang about remembering the works of the LORD and becoming like him, and Psalm 133 pictured the beauty of unity. Chapter 15 gave the resurrection: the gospel of first importance, Christ the firstfruits, the nature of the resurrection body, and the victory over death. Two doctrinal pauses studied the resurrection of Christ and the resurrection of the dead. Chapter 16 closed the letter with the collection, greetings, and the cry “Our Lord, come!”
reflectionQuestions: Paul calls the death and resurrection of Christ “of first importance.” What other things in your spiritual life have crowded into that first place? How can you put the gospel back at the center?
The resurrection of Jesus is the firstfruits of the resurrection of believers. How does knowing your body will be raised change how you see aging, illness, or death?
Paul ends his long letter with “Let all that you do be done in love.” Where in your life this week will it be hardest to do everything in love? What will you ask Christ for help with?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus that he died for your sins and was raised on the third day.
Tell him what you want to hold on to this week.
